trap_ledger.why: Thunderstorms stopped Berlin's departures: an extraordinary circumstance
Left 3 h 5 min late but reached the gate 2 h 48 min late: under three hours at arrival
Cancellation announced on 16 May for 2 June: 17 days' notice, 14 or more owes nothing
A US airline's flight from New York into Lisbon: outside the Regulation's scope
New York to Miami: a flight outside the EU altogether
A strike by French air traffic controllers: extraordinary
A bird strike on the previous landing: extraordinary (C-315/15)
Claim AC-2231 already paid 1,200 euros on 30 September: a second claim is a duplicate
A 300-euro voucher in full and final settlement of a claim worth 1,200 euros in cash

cards.why: LIS-MAD, 503 km; cancelled with 2 days' notice and moved to the next day; a crew shortage is not extraordinary: 3 paying passengers x 250 euros = 750 euros ($825)
LIS-BER, 2,310 km within the EU; at the gate 3 h 41 min late; a hydraulic leak found before departure is not extraordinary: 3 paying passengers x 400 euros = 1,200 euros ($1,320 at $1.10)
BER-LIS, 2,310 km within the EU; 3 h 30 min late at the gate; a strike by Aerolark's own pilots is not extraordinary (C-28/20): 3 x 400 euros = 1,200 euros ($1,320)

Departs Lisbon, so covered on a US airline; 5,410 km; 4 h 20 min late at the gate; a late aircraft held for a repair is technical: 3 passengers including the award ticket x 600 euros = 1,800 euros ($1,980)
